textbookText: Rana tigrina Observe the animal given below and answer the following questions.

i. What are its unique external features? ii. What is the significance of its moist skin? iii. It is mostly aquatic and found in damp places. Why? iv. It is not seen in extreme hot or cold environment? Why? v. What might be its economic importance?
Systematic position Kingdom Phylum Group Sub-phylum Division Super-class Class Genus Species Common name

Rana tigrina is a common frog species found in Asian countries such as Nepal, India Baangladesh, China, Sri lanka etc and is commonly called “Bull frog” or “Asian bull frog”. This species belongs to Ranidae family and distinguished by its characteristic green colouration with black blotches, larger size, conical snout, mid-dorsal white line, vocal sacs (in male for croak) etc. It is found in moist habitats such as forest, farmlands, urban areas although prefer to live in freshwater bodies like pond, lake, river etc. Frogs are cold blooded and they hide in moist burrow to protect from extreme cold days of winter and hot days of summer. Now, its scientific name has been changed to Hoplobatrachus tigerinus. In some countries, they are commercially farmed or hunted for meat. Frogs are the natural predator of insects or pest that can damage our cultivated crops. They have been used in medical and scientific research for centuries because of their physiological similarities to higher vertebrates.

Why is it selected for study? i. It is easily available, inexpensive and non- poisonous. ii. Bull frog is better known than the toad. iii. Its size is appropriate for handling and dissecting in the laboratory. iv. It can be kept alive for few days without feeding. v. Its life cycle is short simple and can be easily observed. vi. It is a sample representative of vertebrates and basically its anatomy is similar to other higher vertebrates including human.

Do you know? Some species of Frogs were previously used in the preganancy test. Injection of women’s urine into the African clawed frog Xenopus resulted production of ova which was the proof of pregnancy. 8.4.2 HABITAT AND HABIT Rana tigrina is commonly found in water or on damp soil. It lives most of the time in moist land rich in green vegetation near fresh water or found swimming in pond, ditches, rivers lakes, streams. It frequently visits water bodies to keep its skin moist for cutaneous respiration. It can escape from enemies by immediately diving into water. While living near aquatic habitat, it can easily access food since plenty of insects, worms, slugs, small frogs etc. are found there. Moreover, it needs water for reproductive activities, and all its embryonic stages including the larval stage are passed in water.

Figure 8.4.1 Frog near water Rana tigrina is a non-poisonous, solitary, harmless and normally silent animal without any armatures. It is a free living, predaceous and cannibalistic animal. Generally, its presence is only detected after it is being disturbed on the banks of ponds, streams, pools, or in the paddy field. Frog is active at the day time and hence called diurnal animal. In breeding season, males are gathered in shallow water in paddy field or ponds and croak. i. Locomotion: In frog, locomotion takes place by leaping on the land and swimming in the water. It has strong and long hind limbs which are contracted in ‘Z’ shaped manner and short forelimbs in upright position during the resting posture. When leaping, it extends hind limbs and leaves the land quickly; throwing body up into the air and body is supported by fore limbs at the time of landing. A frog may leap about 1.5 meter at a jump. While swimming, hind limbs provide powerful backward thrust with their broad webbed toes spreading apart for propelling forward. Left and right fore limbs also support and are moved alternately while swimming.
Figure 8.4.2 Stages of body posture while leaping on land ii. Feeding:

Adult frog is carnivorous and its food chiefly consists of living insects, worms, slugs, small fishes, tadpole etc. It quickly shots out its protrusible and sticky tongue for capturing prey and whole food is, then swallowed without chewing. It prefers to hunt live prey and discards motionless or dead prey as food. Frog is a glutton and hence feed excess; becomes fatty, accumulates reserve food material such as glycogen and fat before going to hibernation.
